name: Betamethasone + Levocetirizine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Kidney dosing follows the levocetirizine component. Levocetirizine is contraindicated in end-stage kidney disease and in patients on hemodialysis, so this combination should not be used in dialysis patients. The registered tablet carries 5 mg levocetirizine with betamethasone; the 2.5 mg regimens the label gives for CrCl 10 to 80 mL/min cannot be given with it, so a fixed-dose tablet does not fit reduced kidney function.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault).

bands.recommendation: CrCl >80: usual dose, 5 mg once daily in the evening. CrCl 50–80 (mild renal impairment): 2.5 mg once daily (label). A fixed-dose tablet fits only CrCl >80. The fixed-dose combination cannot deliver 2.5 mg: use single-ingredient levocetirizine at the label dose.
bands.short: Only if CrCl >80; else single agent

bands.recommendation: CrCl 50–80: 2.5 mg once daily. CrCl 30–50 (moderate renal impairment): 2.5 mg once every other day (label). The fixed-dose combination cannot deliver 2.5 mg: use single-ingredient levocetirizine at the label dose.
CrCl 10–30 (severe renal impairment): 2.5 mg twice weekly, once every 3 to 4 days (label). The fixed-dose combination cannot deliver 2.5 mg: use single-ingredient levocetirizine at the label dose.

CrCl 10–30: 2.5 mg twice weekly (label). The fixed-dose combination cannot deliver 2.5 mg: use single-ingredient levocetirizine at the label dose. CrCl <10 (end-stage renal disease): contraindicated; should not receive levocetirizine (label 4.2).

hd.text: Contraindicated in patients undergoing hemodialysis (label 4.2). Dialysis does not remove it effectively (label 10), so a dose after dialysis does not make it safe.

pd.text: Peritoneal dialysis means end-stage kidney disease, where the label contraindicates levocetirizine (CrCl <10 mL/min, label 4.2).

crrt.text: Not studied (no label data). Specialist input.

dialyzable: No: not effectively removed by dialysis (label 10).
monitoring: Somnolence and fatigue; the risk of adverse reactions is greater with impaired kidney function because levocetirizine is substantially excreted by the kidneys (label 8.6).

pediatric.usual_dose: Ages 6 to 11: 2.5 mg once daily in the evening (do not exceed). Ages 6 months to 5 years: 1.25 mg once daily (do not exceed). Ages 12 and older: adult dosing (label).
pediatric.max_dose: 2.5 mg/day (6 to 11 years); 1.25 mg/day (6 months to 5 years) (label).

renal.recommendation: Contraindicated in children 6 months to 11 years with impaired renal function (label 4.3). Ages 12 and older: adult table.

crrt.text: Not studied; contraindicated with impaired renal function in children 6 months to 11 years (label 4.3).
